$comment: Strings that were corrected on a live surface and must not come back.
This exists because corrected copy has a way of returning. Design plates, drafts and audits are
written against whatever the site said on the day they were made, and porting one months later
silently reinstates every claim fixed since. Website-plateAug11 restates the prize-funding claim
and the draw wording verbatim, and its own README describes a sponsor-funded note the markup does
Each entry names the string, why it was wrong, and the commit that removed it, so a reader who
trips this can read the reasoning rather than guess at it. Matching is whitespace- and
apostrophe-normalised, because JSX splits a sentence across lines and prettier moves the break.
Adding copy that trips a rule here is not a reason to delete the rule. It is a reason to check
whether the claim became true - and if it did, to say so in the entry and remove it deliberately.

patterns: pool's whole staking yield goes to one depositor
whole pool's interest goes to one depositor
prize is funded entirely from the staking yield
Prizes are funded from realised staking yield
Prizes are funded solely from pooled staking yield
prizes come from the pooled staking yield
rules.why: The mechanism is real but it is not what has paid. The harvester has not yet covered a prize and sponsors have funded every draw settled so far. Stating the mechanism as history is the one thing the site's own 'verify it yourself' invitation cannot survive.
rules.instead: Describe the design, then say what has actually funded the draws, next to the figures.

patterns: $10 a year
$10/yr for five characters
costs $10 a year
rules.why: SuiNS charges $10 for the first year and $5 to renew, read from getPriceList() and getRenewalPriceList() on mainnet. '$10 a year' overstates the ongoing cost and contradicted the price table four sections below it on the same page.
rules.instead: Derive the sentence from lib/suins-pricing.ts, which is drift-checked against chain.

patterns: Your competition. Your licence. Our draw.
rules.why: Operator correction: the draw is not ours, it is Sui mainnet's. The organiser holds the licence, the prize and the customer; the chain settles the draw.
rules.instead: Your competition. Your licence. Sui Mainnet Draw.

patterns: then $5/yr
then $50/yr
then $150/yr
rules.why: SuiNS pricing is DAO-mutable on-chain config. A figure typed into a component is a mirror nobody checks, and stale here means quoting a price the registrar will not honour.
rules.instead: SUINS_TIERS in lib/suins-pricing.ts, verified by scripts/verify-suins-prices.mjs.

patterns: describes how the prize is funded — from yield rather than
rules.why: No loss follows from principal never being spent, whatever funds the prize. Explaining it by funding source tied the guarantee to a fact that is currently false.
rules.instead: 'No loss' describes what happens to your principal - it is never spent, whatever funds the prize.

patterns: start at fifteen to forty-five thousand dollars
fifteen to forty-five thousand dollars
below that line there has been nothing
the layer below the audit shouldn't be empty
rules.why: Two unsupportable claims in one sentence on a page that asks to be checked. Of eighteen firms serving Sui, exactly one publishes a price and it starts near seven thousand for a standard review - so a fifteen-thousand floor is falsifiable by any prospect who has asked for a quote. And the layer below is not empty: open-source Move mutation testing exists, is actively maintained, and one engine is Sui-only and already ships as a pull-request action. Sourced in operations/company/sui-foundation-research-2026-08-30.md.
rules.instead: Quote the only published audit prices there are, and claim the difference that survives a hostile reader: the existing tools leave an exit code and a console log, and nobody produces a shareable, attestable, per-commit assurance artifact for Move.

patterns: launch.projectxprotocol.dev
launch.protocolx.io
rules.why: Purged under D-113 and D-114, decided by the operator and executed 8 August 2026. An external audit recommended restoring DNS and serving a retirement page; that reverses a decision this repository has taken.
rules.instead: Nothing. LAUNCHER_URL stays fail-closed and the card does not render.
